reason: The crankshaft will need support on the base, so I’ll start with the bearing frames.
expectation: The frames will attach to the base and provide supports for the turning shaft.

alternatives.reason: The rod and guide also seem useful, but I’d rather start with the base.

effect: The bearings are in place, so the crankshaft can now be fitted.
reason: I'll fit the crankshaft into its bearings to build the turning part of the mechanism.
expectation: The shaft will be supported by the bearings and able to turn.

alternatives.reason: The follower assembly is also needed, but I want to finish the shaft support first.

effect: The crankshaft is turning in the frame, ready for the cam.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: I'll add the off-centre cam to the shaft; it should turn rotation into an up-and-down movement.
expectation: The cam will turn with the shaft, ready to lift a follower, though the follower may need to be fitted separately.

alternatives.reason: The follower and guide are also needed, but I want to finish the rotating assembly first.

effect: The cam's off-centre edge rises and falls as the shaft turns, confirming how it can drive the follower.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the mechanism clearer.
reason: I'll assemble the follower rod and guide; it's the only offered combination and should let the rod move vertically.
expectation: The rod will fit into the guide, ready to follow the cam, though it may need other parts first.

effect: The follower is assembled in its guide and ready to join the cam mechanism.
reason: I'll join the follower to the cam assembly; it's the only offered combination and should connect the rising cam edge to the rod.
expectation: The guided rod will sit against the cam and move up and down as it turns, although it may need the spring to follow it reliably.

effect: The guided follower is now positioned over the cam; it still needs a way to stay in contact and a handle to turn the shaft.
reaction: The parts are coming together predictably.
reason: I'll add the spring so the follower can stay against the cam as it falls.
expectation: The spring will help the rod follow the cam down as well as rise, though the handle will still be needed to turn it.

alternatives.reason: The handle is also needed, but I want to finish the follower first.

effect: The spring is fitted, and the result suggests comparing its pull with an unhooked run when testing.
reaction: I'm curious how much difference the spring makes.
reason: I'll add the handle so I can turn and test the lifter; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The handle will let me turn the cam and observe the follower rise and fall, possibly with a comparison to an unhooked spring.

effect: The test confirmed that the spring keeps the follower against the cam when it might otherwise hang, completing the lifter.
reaction: The comparison made the spring's purpose clear and was satisfying to see.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the lifter with and without the spring was most worthwhile: it showed why the follower needs help following the cam down.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the follower into its guide was straightforward preparation, with little to observe on its own.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the light follower to sometimes hang without the spring's pull.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; the parts had clear roles, though several were straightforward assembly steps.

continue.text: Yes. I'd like to see how this understandable mechanism makes the paper dragon wave.
